newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Blasts heard near Ranariddh loyalist general's home.
newsitem.headline: Blasts heard near Ranariddh loyalist general's home.

text.p: Rifle fire and grenade explosions were heard near the home of a top general loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Saturday.
Witnesses said fighting had erupted for a second time between rival Cambodian government troops on the northwestern outskirts of the city.
"We can hear loud explosions. I think they are B-40 rockets coming from the area of Nhiek Bun Chhay's house," said the reporter. The general is Ranariddh's top military adviser.
The explosions could be heard in central Phnom Penh, some five km (three miles) away.
Witnesses also said troops loyal to Hun Sen appeared to be moving toward a military base controlled by Ranariddh's forces near Phnom Penh airport, about six km (four miles) from the general's home.

Forces loyal to the rival prime ministers clashed near the base earlier on Saturday, but Hun Sen said the fighting did not signal a civil war. The two prime ministers head a deeply divided coalition government formed after United Nations-supervised elections in 1993.
